blockingIssues.description: Replay-range validation only inspects the selected paint-record slice, so primitive-only or partially balanced subranges inside an already-open scoped layer can be reported as successful and replay without the required structural markers. The same defect was also reported from the bundled replay changes reviewed under `scene-family-ordering-and-batching`.

GPUISceneBridge's documented unsupported-style fallback behavior is inconsistent with the implementation and tests: path clips are documented as bounding-rect fallback while code uses a full-surface no-op, and radial/conic gradients are documented as using the gradient start color while code leaves them on `cmd.color`.
The focused bridge test surface does not cover unsupported blend-mode fallback even though VAL-SCENE-011 explicitly requires unsupported blend semantics to degrade through a documented fallback path.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add an explicit worker rule to isolate feature commits to files within the feature's declared scope and verify `extern/zed` remains untouched before a success handoff.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The review for `scene-replay-range-safety` found a referenced feature commit that included an `extern/zed` change despite mission guidance to keep that checkout read-only, and the review for `scene-family-ordering-and-batching` found the submitted feature commit bundled bridge/replay files outside the feature's declared VAL-SCENE-001..005 scope.

rejectedObservations.observation: The scene-replay handoff was stale relative to the transcript skeleton.
The bridge feature handoff recorded `commitId: pending`.
A reviewed feature commit modified `extern/zed` even though mission guidance says it must stay read-only.
